item.title: Sharp quantitative stability of the Hong--Krahn--Szeg\H{o} inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.28757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp quantitative stability estimates for the Hong--Krahn--Szeg\H{o} inequality for arbitrary open sets of positive finite measure in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. In dimensions $d\ge3$, the optimal stability exponent is $(d+2)/2$, while in dimension two the sharp stability modulus is $t^2/\log(e/t)$. These results improve the quantitative stability estimate of Brasco and Pratelli~\cite[Theorem 3.5]{BP} and resolve Open Problem 7.56 of Brasco and De Philippis~\cite[Open Problem 7.56]{BDP}.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou

item.title: Strong gradient absorption and initial decay prevent blow-up
item.description: arXiv:2610.28913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider positive classical solutions of the Cauchy problem for $u_t-\Delta u=u^p-\mu|\nabla u|^q$, with sufficiently smooth initial data $u_0$, in the strong absorption regime, namely $q\ge p>1$ and $\mu>0$. It has remained a long standing open problem whether finite time blow-up can occur if $u_0$ decays at space infinity. We here solve this problem, showing that the answer in negative. To this end, we establish a novel, universal Bernstein-type gradient estimate, of independent interest, valid only in the range $q\ge p$. Moreover, the decay assumption on $u_0$ turns out to be essentially optimal. Indeed we show that the solution blows up in finite time whenever $u_0$ has a positive limit at infinity, and we determine the blow-up behavior of $u$ at space infinity under an additional assumption.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Souplet, Berikbol T. Torebek

item.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.29000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.
item.dc:creator: Yunhong Deng

item.title: A Jump-Modified Wasserstein Gradient Flow for Maximum Mean Discrepancy with Energy Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.29007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a jump-modified Wasserstein gradient flow of the squared maximum mean discrepancy generated by the energy kernels $K(z)=-|z|^q$, $0<q<2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$ as well as the one-dimensional range $1\le q<2$. Under subcritical density and finite-moment assumptions, we prove global well-posedness. The added jumps transfer mass toward smaller values of the first variation and dissipate the same MMD energy as the transport term. Under our hypotheses on the target and jump rates, every Borel probability measure with finite MMD energy and zero jump dissipation is equal to the target. Combining this rigidity with compactness and a second-moment identity yields convergence to the target from finite-second-moment data, without additional uniform-in-time density or moment assumptions. We also construct a global collision-free particle process whose energy is nonincreasing along each path. A quantitative mean-field estimate applies to general initial empirical approximations, including deterministic configurations; propagation of chaos for exchangeable data and long-time target approximation follow as consequences.
item.dc:creator: Ansh Desai, Jason Liu, Srujan Roplekar, Matthew Rosenzweig

item.title: A logarithmic regularity criterion for the axisymmetric Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For axisymmetric solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb R^3$, the circulation $\Gamma=ru^\theta$ obeys a maximum principle, and the resulting a priori bound on $\Gamma$ is scale-invariant. Nonetheless, the global regularity problem remains completely open. The sharpest known regularity criteria in terms of the circulation are slightly subcritical, namely $|\Gamma|\lesssim(\log r^{-1})^{-k}$ near the symmetry axis; Lei and Zhang proved regularity for $k=2$, and Wei later lowered the exponent to $k=3/2$. In this note, we strengthen the criterion further to $k=5/4$. The argument follows the usual route of energy estimates for the quantities $\omega^r/r$ and $\omega^\theta/r$, but now with a sharper bound on the vortex stretching term in the equation for $\omega^r/r$, in which the loss is proportional only to the square root of the number of scales between the inner vortex core and the far field.
item.dc:creator: Stan Palasek

item.title: Time-periodic solutions of an SIS epidemic model
item.description: arXiv:2610.29062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of strictly positive, nonstationary time-periodic solutions for the spatially heterogeneous SIS epidemic model with standard incidence. On a bounded interval with Neumann boundary conditions, we construct smooth, time-independent transmission and recovery rates satisfying \(\beta(x)>\gamma(x)>0\), together with diffusion coefficients \(d_I>d_S>0\), such that periodic solutions coexist with the unique endemic equilibrium for every prescribed positive total population. Thus, pointwise dominance of transmission over recovery does not ensure convergence to equilibrium. Our approach combines an inverse construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium with a coefficient path that preserves both the equilibrium and the pointwise inequalities. A change in the number of unstable eigenvalues along this path yields small-amplitude periodic solutions through a center-manifold reduction and a generalized Hopf bifurcation argument. The proof uses an AI-assisted construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium under the pointwise condition $\beta>\gamma>0$.
item.dc:creator: Fang Li, Pengfei Song, Kexin Zhang, Maolin Zhou

item.title: Inviscid Limit Problem for Radially Symmetric Stationary States of Viscous and Heat-Conductive Ideal Gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.29074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the zero-viscosity limit of radially symmetric stationary solutions for the inflow and outflow problems for a viscous and heat-conductive polytropic ideal gas in the exterior of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \geq 3$), under prescribed boundary and far-field conditions. The far-field velocity is assumed to be zero, and the solutions are considered in a sufficiently small neighborhood of the far-field state. In the zero-viscosity limit, the viscous terms disappear from the momentum equation, while the heat-conduction term remains in the energy equation. For the outflow problem, we prove that the viscous stationary solution converges uniformly to the corresponding stationary solution of the heat-conductive inviscid system, with convergence rate $O(\mu)$. For the inflow problem, a boundary layer appears near the inner boundary. We show that the viscous stationary solution is uniformly approximated by the superposition of the limiting stationary solution and a boundary-layer profile. Here, the boundary layer appears only for the density and velocity, whereas no boundary-layer appears for the temperature. Moreover, for any $\alpha \in (0,1)$, the approximation error is of order $O(\mu^\alpha)$.
item.dc:creator: Itsuko Hashimoto

item.title: Isolated Singularities of k-Hessian Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify isolated singularities of nonpositive, $k$-admissible classical solutions to $k$-Hessian equations without radial symmetry assumptions. For $1\le k<n/2$, we consider $F_k[u]=(-u)^p$ with $1<p\le nk/(n-2k)$. Below the Serrin exponent, we obtain fundamental-solution asymptotics and characterize removability by the vanishing of the leading coefficient. At the Serrin exponent, we determine the exact logarithmic correction and its universal coefficient for every nonremovable singularity. In the critical dimension $k=n/2$, we establish logarithmic asymptotics and a removability criterion for $F_k[u]=f(x,u,\nabla u)$ with continuous sources satisfying $0\le f(x,s,\xi)\le C|\xi|^\ell e^{-\alpha s}$, where $\alpha>0$ and $0\le\ell<n$. The proofs combine Hessian-measure compactness, Wolff-potential estimates, a global B\^ocher theorem, and a bounded-variation analysis of spherical extrema.
item.dc:creator: Shiguang Ma, Shengyang Zang

item.title: Isolated singularities of certain quasi-linear elliptic inequalities II
item.description: arXiv:2610.29113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of isolated singularities for quasilinear elliptic equations of $p$-Laplacian type. We focus on the $p$-Laplace equation with the critical Serrin exponent $n(p-1)/(n-p)$ and the $n$-Laplace equation with critical exponential growth. We prove that any positive solution either admits a $C^{1,\alpha}$ extension to the origin or exhibits a precise singular asymptotic behavior. These results provide a complement to our previous study on $p$-Laplacian type inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Shiguang Ma, Shengyang Zang

item.title: Partial regularity of heat flow of fractional harmonic maps to spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.29191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notation of stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps from $\R^m$ into the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{\ell-1}\hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^\ell$, for $0<s<1$, framed through the parabolic version of Caffarelli-Silvestre's extension. We prove that any stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps is smooth away from a closed set of vanishing $(m+2-2s)$-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This extends to the fractional settings the partial regularity theorem on the heat flow of harmonic maps into spheres by Chen-Li-Lin and Feldman.
item.dc:creator: Hengrong Du, Tao Huang, Armin Schikorra, Changyou Wang

item.title: Sharp asymptotics for a free boundary touching a degenerate boundary: the perpetual Heston put
item.description: arXiv:2610.29253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the exercise boundary of the perpetual American put in the Heston model near zero variance. There the pricing operator degenerates, and the exercise boundary, a free boundary in the stock--variance half-plane, touches the boundary of the half-plane. No Feller condition is imposed. The boundary is analytic at positive variance and extends as a regular $C^1$ curve tangent to the zero-variance axis. Its approach to the axis follows one of three laws, according to whether the Feller ratio $2\kappa\theta/\sigma^2$ is larger than, equal to, or smaller than one: a logarithmic correction to linear order, an exponential correction in the square root of the logarithm, or a fractional power. In the first two cases the leading coefficients are explicit and the tangent is not H\"older continuous at the axis. In the third case the exponent is selected by a possibly nonsymmetric stable operator on the axis, and the amplitude is finite and positive.
item.dc:creator: Takwon Kim, Junkee Jeon, Jehan Oh

item.title: Scattering in spacetime cones for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.29265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$, with a class of `mixed' nonlinearities that admit soliton solutions. We are interested in the long-time behaviour of solutions with finite, but possibly large, mass and/or energy. By a spacetime cone, we mean an open set in $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}_{x,t}$ that is invariant under dilation $(x, t) \mapsto (\alpha x, \alpha t)$ for all $\alpha > 0$. Our main result is as follows: let $u(x, t)$ be the solution with initial condition in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Let $\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}$ be the mass and energy of $u$, and let $\eta = \eta(\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}) > 0$ be sufficiently small. Let $C_\epsilon$ be the complement of $N \geq 1$ of sufficiently thin spacetime cones $\{ (x, t) \mid |x-v_jt| \leq \epsilon t \}$, where $v_1, \dots, v_N$ are fixed velocities and $\epsilon$ is sufficiently small. If the $L^\infty$ norm of $u$ in $C_\epsilon$ is $\leq \eta$, we prove that $u$ scatters in $C_{2\epsilon} \subset C_\epsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hassell, Qiuye Jia, Xiaoxu Wu

item.title: On finite-dimensional attractor to 2D incompressible fluid with stress-diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.29290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider incompressible visco-elastic rate-type fluid flow, with the Cauchy stress defined in terms of positive-definite symmetric tensor $B$. The tensor $B$ obeys an evolution equation, combining Oldroyd-B and Giesekus model, and, crucially, a diffusion term. Restricting ourselves to the 2D periodic problem, we show existence of a finite-dimensional global attractor. We also estimate its dimension explicitely in terms of the equation parameters.
item.dc:creator: Dalibor Pra\v{z}\'ak

item.title: Effective stability and sharp logarithmic time scales for Hamiltonian PDEs on the circle
item.description: arXiv:2610.29307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove effective stability and matching logarithmic upper bounds for small solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs on the one-dimensional torus. An analytic coefficient-majorant calculus and an explicit normal-form iteration yield stability times with logarithms of order $L^{1+1/p}/(\log L)^{1/p}$ for Gevrey weights and $L^{1+(q-1)/(pq+1)}$ for logarithmic ultra-differentiable weights, where $L=\log(1/\varepsilon)$ and $p\geq1$ measures the order dependence of the small divisors. Even frequencies are organized into the exact blocks $\{n,-n\}$; elementary frequency gaps and constant weights on these blocks close the energy estimate. We verify the hypotheses for convolution NLS, fractional NLS with every fixed noninteger exponent $\eta>1/2$, and a beam equation with a metric parameter and a variational gradient nonlinearity. Two fixed analytic nonlocal Hamiltonian PDEs admit finite-support solutions whose first prescribed norm amplification occurs on the same logarithmic scales along sequences $\varepsilon_n\to0$. The common lower theorem applies to every sufficiently small datum of each admissible equation. Its combination with these examples establishes sharpness of both regularity-dependent scales under the same analytic and arithmetic hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Bingqi Yu, Yong Li

item.title: Upper and lower bounds for heat kernels with very strong degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2610.29325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the following degenerate parabolic equation on a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^d$ containing $0$: $\partial_t u - \nabla\cdot(\varphi(t, x) \nabla u)= 0$, where $\varphi$ is a rough weight behaving like $|x|^\theta$ near $0$ for some $\theta \geq 2$, and $u$ satisfies Neumann boundary condition. We prove that this equation admits a heat kernel with upper and lower Gaussian-type bounds.
item.dc:creator: Hector Bouton

item.title: An Arnold-Type Stability Analysis of Vortex Filaments
item.description: arXiv:2610.29353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish nonlinear orbital stability of circular arcs with opening angle $\theta\le \pi$ and closed circles under the Localized Induction Equation (LIE), with prescribed endpoint constraints for arcs. Our Arnold-type variational approach combines two conserved quantities, the bending energy and a component of the fluid impulse, into a functional that we prove is comparable to the squared $H^2$-distance from the corresponding orbit for all admissible curves. For circular arcs with angle $\theta>\pi$, we prove nonlinear orbital instability using the inverse generalized Hasimoto transformation.
item.dc:creator: Masashi Aiki, Mitsuo Higaki

item.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(\lambda,p) = \sup_{\substack{ u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} (|\nabla u|^2+u^2)\,dx\le 1 }} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \left(e^{4\pi u^2}-1-\lambda |u|^p\right)\,dx, \qquad p\ge 2. \] Building on the classification away from the thresholds by Chen, Jiang, Lu and Zhu (2026), we resolve the endpoint cases: both thresholds for $p=2$ and the finite threshold for $2<p\le4$ are attained. We also prove compactness of centred radial extremals and one-sided value expansions governed by the selected endpoint $L^p$ mass. For $p>4$, we quantify how extremals spread out as $\lambda\to\infty$ by establishing the two-term expansion \[ S(\lambda,p)=4\pi+\mathcal C_p\lambda^{-2/(p-4)} +D_p\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting variational problem at unit $L^2$ mass. An explicit correction involving the sixth moment and the full $H^1$ normalization determines $D_p$ and selects the limiting maximizers. Rescaled centred radial extremals converge strongly to these profiles in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ along subsequences. For every fixed $\lambda>\lambda_*(4)$, we further establish \[ \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(\lambda,p)-4\pi\bigr) =2\log\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}}{\lambda}<0, \] where $\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local critical penalty determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. The gradient energy has the same logarithmic rate, and the centred radial profiles, normalized in mass and gradient energy, converge along subsequences to sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg optimizers. An exact transfer identity extends these endpoint and asymptotic results to every constant planar norm.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Guo, Yanjun Liu

item.title: A spinor-adapted geometric approach to nonlinear Dirac systems on the Schwarzschild black hole background
item.description: arXiv:2610.29406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on our previous work, we extend the spinor-adapted geometric method for nonlinear Dirac systems from small perturbations of Minkowski spacetime to the Schwarzschild background. As a linear foundation, we establish integrated local energy decay estimates and an \(r^p\)-weighted energy hierarchy for spinor fields, adapting the physical-space approach of Dafermos and Rodnianski to the Dirac setting. The main focus of the paper is nonlinear. We consider a semilinear tensorial wave--Dirac model motivated by the wave-gauge reduction of the Einstein--Dirac system and prove global small-data stability. A principal difficulty is the apparent loss of derivatives arising from the coupling between the first-order Dirac equation and the second-order tensorial wave equation. We overcome this difficulty through a spinor-adapted energy hierarchy that exploits the complementary roles of the Dirac-current energy and the spinorial wave energy. In particular, the nonlinear estimates are closed without requiring the top-order Dirac-current estimate. The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. The combination of Dirac-current energy, spinorial wave energy, Kosmann Lie derivatives, and the Clifford-algebraic null structure enables us to close the nonlinear estimates without imposing an independent null condition on the tensorial wave equation. Thus, the nonlinear closure relies fundamentally on structures intrinsic to the Dirac equation. A second main result is the global small-data stability of the Maxwell--Dirac system in the Lorenz gauge on the Schwarzschild background, under a vanishing-charge assumption. This extends the nonlinear stability theory to a genuine gauge-coupled Dirac system and demonstrates the applicability of the spinor-adapted physical-space approach beyond the tensorial wave--Dirac model.
item.dc:creator: Seokchang Hong

item.title: Local well-posedness, blow-up phenomenon and ill-posedness for a model system of the radiating gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.29462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Cauchy problem for a model system of radiating gas in multi-dimensional space. Firstly, we prove that the model is locally well-posed in Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $s>1+\frac{d}{p}$ (resp., $s=1+\frac{d}{p}$, $r=1$), including the endpoint space $B^1_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Secondly, we show that the data-to-solution map is not uniformly continuous on bounded subsets of these Besov spaces. Moreover, we construct a blow-up scenario and derive two sufficient blow-up conditions, which improve the previous blow-up condition obtained in \cite{MR3016436}. Finally, we prove that the Cauchy problem is ill-posed in the critical space $B^{1+\frac{d}{p}}_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $r>1$ in the sense of norm inflation.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen, Zhaonan Luo, Yuchen Yang, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Maximal velocity estimates for Hardy operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.29513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove maximal velocity estimates for the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator, and possibly external potentials. As an application, we give another proof of the nonexistence of the wave operator intertwining Hardy operators with and without long-range perturbations with Coulomb decay.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Ishida, Konstantin Merz

item.title: $L^p$-Liouville properties and realizations of Schr\"odinger operators on incomplete Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.29514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of the paper is to highlight and standardize in a self-contained framework the connections between some properties associated with the Laplace-Beltrami operator on possibly incomplete Riemannian manifolds. We present both new and well-known characterizations of the positivity-preserving property, essential self-adjointness, and Liouville-type results for $L^2$-functions, using the latter to establish a clear hierarchy among these properties. Furthermore, we prove the stability of the essential self-adjointness of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on incomplete Riemannian manifolds under the removal of closed (possibly non-compact) subsets from a complete manifold, subject to suitable conditions on their (generalized) Hausdorff measure. With appropriate modifications, this framework is adapted throughout the paper to the general $L^p$-case for $p\in (1,+\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Bisterzo, Salvatore Lincastri, Giona Veronelli

item.title: Harnack-type inequalities for nonlocal parabolic equations in the upper fast-diffusion range
item.description: arXiv:2610.29553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study non-negative weak solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear nonlocal parabolic equations of the form $$ (u^q)_t+\mathcal Lu=0, $$ where $\mathcal L$ is a nonlocal $p$-Laplace-type operator with a symmetric measurable kernel. We consider the fast-diffusion range $1<p<q+1$ and establish Harnack-type estimates in the upper fast-diffusion regime $\widetilde p_c<p<q+1$, where $\widetilde p_c$ is a critical exponent determined by the interplay between the temporal nonlinearity and the nonlocal diffusion. In particular, the estimates apply to the nonlocal parabolic $p$-Laplace equation and the nonlocal porous medium equation.
item.dc:creator: Mariia Savchenko, Igor Skrypnik, Yevgeniia Yevgenieva

item.title: Global existence for the semilinear regular Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation, II
item.description: arXiv:2610.29623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our previous work [25], we established the global existence of solutions to the semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation with power nonlinearity \(|u|^p\) in the case where the damping term dominates the mass term. In contrast, this paper studies the reverse case, namely, the existence of global solutions to the equation when the mass term dominates the damping term. We prove that small-data solutions exist globally if \[ p>\max\{p_0((m+1)n,\mu), \widetilde{p}_1(n,m,\mu)\} \] for \(\delta\doteq(\mu-1)^2-4\nu^2\leq0\), where \(\delta\) measures the relative dominance between the damping and mass terms, \(p_0(n,\mu)\) is the \textit{Strauss-related} exponent defined by (1.12), and \(\widetilde{p}_1(n,m,\mu)\) is defined by (2.5).
item.dc:creator: Yuequn Li, Fei Guo

item.title: Sharp Brezis--Merle Inequalities for Polyharmonic Dirichlet Problems: Extremal Measures and Critical Asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2610.29626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the Brezis--Merle inequality for very weak solutions of polyharmonic Dirichlet problems with integrable data on smooth bounded domains in conformal dimensions. The inequality is sharp both with respect to the admissible range of the exponent and to the quantity appearing on the right-hand side, which is characterized as the maximum of an associated one-pole Green functional. The supremum defining this quantity is not attained by any integrable datum, but remains unchanged when the admissible class is extended to Radon probability measures; in this enlarged class, the extremals are Dirac masses, and their concentration points are characterized in terms of the associated Green function. On the unit ball, we prove uniqueness of the extremal measure and obtain an explicit optimal bound extending the sharp result for the Laplacian. Finally, we determine the critical asymptotics of the sharp constant on the right-hand side and show that the possible limiting concentration points are selected by the maximum points of the polyharmonic Robin function.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Marcos do \'O, Federica Sani, Victor Rafael Silva

item.title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
item.description: arXiv:2610.29704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.
item.dc:creator: Zakaria Fattah, Ilias Ftouhi, Giorgio Saracco

item.title: Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.29721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.
item.dc:creator: Phillip Harris, Jiaqi Hou, Xiaoqi Huang

item.title: Recovering the reaction coefficient in a time-fractional diffusion equation with variable coefficients in any spatial dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.29763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the inverse problem of determining the reaction coefficient $q(x',t)$ in the time-fractional diffusion equation ${}^CD_t u-Lu+q(x',t)u=f$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,T]$, $x=(x',x_n)$, $0<\alpha<1$, from the trace of the solution on the hyperplane $\{x_n=0\}$. Here ${}^CD_t$ is the Gerasimov--Caputo derivative and $L$ is a uniformly elliptic second-order operator with variable, $x_n$-independent coefficients and without zero-order term. For $L=\Delta$ this problem was studied in dimensions $n=1,2,3$ by methods based on pointwise bounds of the kernels, which are not available for $n\ge4$. Our approach relies on the Eidelman--Kochubei fundamental solution: although its singularity on the diagonal depends on the dimension, we show that it satisfies integral bounds of the same form for all $n\ge1$. Using these bounds, we prove existence, uniqueness and stability of regular solutions of the direct problem with a H\"{o}lder continuous reaction coefficient. Without assuming additional smoothness of the solution, we show that the inverse problem is equivalent to a closed system of integral equations for $q$ and the derivatives $\partial_{x_n}u$, $\partial^2_{x_n}u$. For the inverse problem we establish a conditional Lipschitz stability estimate on the whole time interval and global uniqueness in every dimension, and prove local existence of a solution. In the case $a_{in}\equiv0$, $b_n\equiv0$ we obtain a stability estimate with explicit constants, which reduces to the known estimates for the Laplacian. An explicit two-dimensional example with a mixed coefficient and a normal drift shows that the hypotheses of the main theorems are compatible and that the corresponding terms in the trace condition cannot be omitted.
item.dc:creator: D. K. Durdiev

item.title: Elliptic rearrangement for Poisson equations with mean-zero data
item.description: arXiv:2610.29783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $L^p$ norm of a sign-changing Dirichlet solution of Poisson's equation is shown to be bounded by the maximum of the $L^p$ norms of the ball solutions obtained by signed rearrangement of the source and its negative, assuming the source term has mean value zero. This paired comparison on bounded open sets extends Talenti's elliptic rearrangement principle to solutions that change sign. In dimensions one and two, the paired comparison holds for all $1\le p\le\infty$, and it holds in every dimension for $p=\infty$. The inequalities are sharp and equality cases are characterized. In dimensions $n \geq 3$, paired comparison can fail for every finite $p$ although it remains valid for $p\ge(3n-1)/4$ in the special case of bang-bang sources with mean zero. The mean-zero source assumption is crucial when $p<\infty$. Without it, paired comparison can fail even for bang-bang sources. For sources of arbitrary mean in one dimension, however, the $L^\infty$ paired comparison still holds and so does a comparison for $L^p$ norms of the derivative when $1\le p\le3$.
item.dc:creator: Dorin Bucur, Richard S. Laugesen

item.title: A Super-Convergent Quasi-Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Advection-Diffusion Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.29818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of the present study is to develop discontinuous Galerkin and nonconforming finite-element methods for solving the 2D advection-diffusion equation. The discrete formulations are stabilized by means of a family of numerical fluxes and the dispersion relations are constructed via a Fourier/stability analysis. The linear discontinuous P1DG and non conforming P1NC Galerkin discretizations are studied. A long time stability result is proven for the P1NC and P1DG schemes and fluxes examined here by inspecting the discrete frequencies, solutions of the dispersion relations. A super-convergent result is also demonstrated for the P1NC discrete frequency (O(h 4 ) accuracy) compared to the P1DG one (O(h 2 ) accuracy). These results are in line with those obtained in a previous paper for the shallow-water system.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Y Le Roux (UCBL, ICJ, MMCS)

item.title: Time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for viscous-dispersive heat-conducting compressible fluids
item.description: arXiv:2610.29859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg (NSFK) system, which describes the dynamics of viscous, heat-conducting, compressible fluids with internal capillarity. We prove that, for the adiabatic exponent $\gamma\in(1,2]$, the solution to the NSFK system converges uniformly in space, as time tends to infinity, to a composite wave consisting of a rarefaction wave, a viscous contact wave, and a viscous-dispersive shock with a time-dependent shift, provided that the initial perturbation and the strengths of the contact wave and the shock are sufficiently small. In particular, we do not impose any smallness condition on the strength of the rarefaction wave. Because of the capillarity, the shock is viscous-dispersive and its profile equation is of third order. We treat the shock by the method of $a$-contraction with shifts introduced by Kang and Vasseur. This is the first result on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous-dispersive shock, and of a generic Riemann solution, for the NSFK system.
item.dc:creator: Sungho Han, Jeongho Kim

item.title: Sharp Moser-Onofri inequality on the CR sphere under zero-moment constraints and its application to the stability of the CR Moser-Onofri inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.29877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. By combining a decomposition into low and high spherical harmonics with the known CR localization estimates, we first prove the existence of extremals of the subcritical Moser--Onofri inequality under zero-moment constraints. We then derive their Euler--Lagrange equation, establish their smoothness, and eliminate the moment multiplier by means of the infinitesimal CR conformal action. Using the summation identity (4.9) on the Hardy space $H^2(B^n)$, we show that the extremals of subcritical Moser-Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints are constants. By a limiting argument, we deduce the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. As an application, we establish the stability of Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere with the best stability constant.
item.dc:creator: Lu Chen, Guozhen Lu

item.title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.29914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.
item.dc:creator: R\'emi Buffe, Alessandro Duca, Hugo Parada

item.title: Normal form approach to unconditional well-posedness of the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with an additive noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.29935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a stochastic normal form method for stochastic dispersive equations. As a model example, we study the stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation (SKdV) with an additive noise, posed on the circle. By replacing integration by parts (in time) in the deterministic setting with Ito's product formula in the current stochastic setting, we transform SKdV with an additive noise into a stochastic normal form equation with additive and multiplicative noises. We then use the stochastic normal form equation to prove optimal pathwise unconditional global well-posedness of SKdV in $L^2(\mathbb{T})$.
item.dc:creator: Damiano Greco, Tadahiro Oh, Philippe Sosoe, Yuzhao Wang

item.title: A PDE-theory-guided neural operator and the long-time relaxation of the two-dimensional anisotropic Boussinesq system
item.description: arXiv:2610.29938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design a neural operator for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system with anisotropic dissipation on the periodic box, guided by a rigorous analysis of its long-time behavior. The operator maps a small perturbation of hydrostatic equilibrium, of amplitude $\varepsilon$, to the vorticity at a late time. We prove that the flow relaxes to a stratified shear flow, with the horizontally averaged vorticity staying within $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of its initial value $\bar\omega_0$ and the oscillation about it of order $\varepsilon$. Accordingly, the network outputs $\bar\omega_0$ plus these two parts, each scaled to its size, which grows as $\varepsilon^2$ and $\varepsilon$, respectively. Without this guidance the training either does not converge or misses the $\varepsilon^2$ growth. With it, one network reproduces, sample by sample on $2\times10^3$ test runs over a factor of $23$ in amplitude, the quantity bounded by the theorem to a median error of $2.2$ percent. Being fast and differentiable with respect to the initial data, the network is also used to search the space of initial data, and with every candidate checked by the solver the search finds initial data for which this quantity is $4.4$ times the largest value among the test runs, raising the lower bound for the constant of the theorem by that factor.
item.dc:creator: Akram Moustafa, Jiahong Wu, Xiaoming Zheng

item.title: Saturating spaces for the squared-gradient nonlinearity on compact Riemannian manifolds via Nash embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.29952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the saturation property on smooth compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary. Starting from a finite-dimensional space of smooth functions, one considers successive iterations of the nonlinear map $f\mapsto|\nabla_g f|_g^2$ and convex combinations. We extend to the general setting of compact manifolds existing results on particular geometries, namely the torus, spheres and Lie groups. Our approach relies on the existence of an isometric embedding of the manifold into $\mathbb{R}^n$ due to Nash. As an application, we obtain global approximate controllability in arbitrarily small time for the bilinear Schr\"odinger equation on any connected compact Riemannian manifold, with finitely many potentials.
item.dc:creator: Buffe R\'emi, Duca Alessandro, Parada Hugo

item.title: Rigidity of the ball for Hartree-type energies and second shape derivative via a continuity argument
item.description: arXiv:2610.29958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the second shape derivative of an optimal design functional involving a nonlocal term in order to prove rigidity of the ball. Our approach relies on a continuity argument that relates the second variation to that of the corresponding local problem. The model serves as a prototype for a broader class of shape optimization problems to which the same strategy may be adapted.
item.dc:creator: Dario Mazzoleni, Riccardo Moraschi, Berardo Ruffini

item.title: Nonlinear Inviscid Damping of Couette Flow with Vorticity Perturbations Supported up to the Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.29975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish nonlinear inviscid damping of the near-Couette flows in a finite channel, with vorticity perturbations vanishing to infinite order at the boundary. To study the boundary effect, we decompose the vorticity into dyadic layers whose supports expand toward the boundary, and use an inductive Newton scheme to track nonlinear interactions across layers. Finally, precise elliptic estimates are established to quantify the velocity generated by different layers.
item.dc:creator: Siming He, Sameer Iyer, Weiren Zhao

item.title: On the strict approximation of currents and space-time trajectories
item.description: arXiv:2610.29981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work establishes a wide variety of strict approximation results for space-time trajectories, a class of space-time currents that are used to model the evolution of dislocations in crystalline materials. In particular, we introduce a strict-type notion of convergence which respects quantities associated with geometric transport phenomena and prove approximation results in this topology. These results build on the classical strict approximation results for normal and integral currents developed by Federer and Fleming, which we also review and refine.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Bonicatto, Filip Rindler, Harry Turnbull

item.title: Long-time dynamics of viscous Gr\"obli triangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.30038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1877 Gr\"obli discovered that three point vortices in the plane can move self-similarly, forming a triangle that rotates while either expanding indefinitely or collapsing in finite time. We study the viscous counterpart of these configurations, namely the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes evolution starting from three point vortices arranged in a Gr\"obli triangle. In the expanding case, viscosity spreads the vortex cores at the same rate as the triangle grows, so the vortices remain well separated relative to their size. Building on this observation, we show that at high Reynolds number the solution stays close to three Lamb--Oseen vortices centered near the vertices of the inviscid triangle for times that grow exponentially with a power of the Reynolds number. In the collapsing case, the same description holds up to times close to the inviscid collision. As an application of the long-time result in the expanding case, we obtain a vanishing viscosity realization of the vortex burst, a nonuniqueness mechanism for point vortices in which a single vortex splits into an expanding Gr\"obli triangle.
item.dc:creator: Michele Dolce, Antonio Tirotta

item.title: A well-posedness theory for the 2D inhomogeneous incompressible Euler equations and a class of global-in-time solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the 2D inhomogeneous incompressible Euler equations. We show that the Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in a class of $m$-fold symmetric functions at critical regularity and allowing the velocity field to grow linearly at spatial infinity. This was a problem posed by P.L. Lions in the homogeneous, not necessarily symmetric case. A key ingredient is a variable-coefficient elliptic theory developed using quasiconformal mappings and Schauder estimates in certain scale-invariant H\"{o}lder spaces. Local well-posedness allows us to derive the one-dimensional system on $\mathbb{S}^1$ satisfied by solutions with $0$-homogeneous vorticity and density. For this system, we can obtain global well-posedness for a class of initial data away from equilibrium. We are unaware of any previous nonperturbative class of time-dependent solutions to the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations for which global well-posedness has been established. Finally, for some signed global solutions, we show a dichotomy between density homogenization and averaged relaxation in infinite time.
item.dc:creator: Ibrahim Suleiman

item.title: Boundary-Driven Nonequilibrium for the Coulomb Landau Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a nonlinear theory of the Coulomb Landau equation in smooth bounded domains with non-isothermal diffuse reflection. We construct a stationary state, prove its perturbative uniqueness and global nonlinear stability, and establish exponential convergence when the wall temperature approaches its stationary profile exponentially. We also establish stationary and global nonlinear well-posedness for prescribed inflow, together with asymptotic stability. The analysis combines a critical kinetic integrability gain with finite-exponent velocity-gradient estimates near grazing, allowing the nonlinear Coulomb estimates to close without $L_x^\infty$ control of velocity gradients.
item.dc:creator: Chanwoo Kim, Jinsol Seo

item.title: On ABP Estimates for a Class of Fully Nonlinear Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.30112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an Alexandrov-Bakelman-Pucci type estimate for a class of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with singular or degenerate coefficients and nonlinear dependence on the gradient. The estimate bounds sub-solutions in terms of their boundary values and weighted integrals of the data. It holds for classical sub-solutions and for viscosity sub-solutions with locally Lipschitz gradients. The assumptions allow general rates of growth in the gradient, with a smallness condition on the data when the associated gradient weight has finite integral. The proof uses the classical weighted contact-set argument. As applications, we obtain sup-norm estimates for viscosity sub-solutions to a class of generalized Monge-Amp\`ere equations, Hessian equations, Hessian quotients under an additional condition on the contact Hessian, and anisotropic mean-curvature-type equations.
item.dc:creator: Junyuan Fang, Jack Peltier, Tuoc Phan

item.title: Free boundary minimal hypersurfaces of Morse index one in Eucildean half-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.28824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a half-space of RN, with nonempty boundary is a higher-dimensional half-catenoid. We also prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a quarter-space is the higher-dimensional quarter-catenoid.
item.dc:creator: Junzhang Li

item.title: BCC optimality for the three-dimensional Coulomb lattice energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.29732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the renormalized Coulomb energy among three-dimensional Bravais lattices of fixed covolume, up to orthogonal transformations. Using Ewald summation, we write the energy, to within an additive constant, as a sum of two positive, rapidly convergent series in real and reciprocal space. Their positivity provides finite lower bounds for all competitors. A passage to the dual lattice reduces the problem to a face-centered cubic comparison. A short basis vector estimate, a certified local Hessian, and interval bounds on a compact five-dimensional domain complete the computer-assisted proof.
item.dc:creator: C. B. Muratov, M. Novaga

item.title: Rayleigh's conjecture for vibrating plates: simpler planar proof and nonlinear extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a simpler proof of Nadirashvili's theorem (Rayleigh's conjecture) that among vibrating clamped plates of prescribed area in the plane, the disk has the lowest fundamental tone. The proof uses a one-shot Talenti type comparison for sign-changing solutions of the Poisson equation with mean-zero data, established in a companion paper. The comparison considers just two rearranged sources, rather than optimizing over all admissible sources as in the traditional two-ball technique. This ``paired comparison'' simplification yields immediate nonlinear extensions: the disk minimizes the clamped quotient $\|\Delta u\|_q/\|u\|_p$ among bounded open sets of prescribed area, for every $1\le p,q\le\infty$. Equality is characterized for $q>1$, while exceptional behavior at $q=1$ is identified. In higher dimensions, we prove ball minimality for $p=\infty$ and conjecture minimality for all $p,q$ within the compact embedding range. We also establish the corresponding interval inequality in one dimension.
item.dc:creator: Dorin Bucur, Richard S. Laugesen

item.title: Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ \Gamma=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Weimin Sheng, Ye Zhu

item.title: A variational construction for Einstein metrics on connected sums of $S^2\times S^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each positive integer $n$, we give a variational construction of a positive Einstein metric on the connected sum of $n$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$, with coupled toric and dihedral symmetries. More precisely, we obtain these metrics via a min-max construction for the total scalar curvature, which is in some sense dual to the usual max-min formulation of the smooth Yamabe invariant within this symmetry class, with more favorable analytic properties.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Chun-Pong Chu, Daniel Stern

item.title: Small-time approximate controllability of bilinear Schr\"odinger equations on compact normal homogeneous spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove small-time global approximate controllability in $L^2$ for bilinear Schr\"odinger equations on compact connected normal homogeneous spaces. The controls act through finitely many smooth real-valued potentials. We first construct finite saturating families on compact connected Lie groups endowed with bi-invariant metrics, using Peter-Weyl theory and the Casimir operator. Their phase saturation contains the representative algebra and is therefore dense in $L^2$. We extend this construction to normal homogeneous quotients using finite generation of the algebra of highest-weight functions. Global controllability follows by combining the phase-to-gradient transport argument of [8] with the gradient generation theorem of [23] and Moser's transport of positive densities.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Parada

item.title: Convergence of solutions to the $p$-Laplace evolution equation as $p$ goes to 1
item.description: arXiv:1103.0229v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the set of solutions to the parabolic singular $p$-Laplace equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ for all space dimensions is continuous in the parameter $p\in [1,+\infty)$ and the initial data. The highly singular limit case $p=1$ is included. In particular, we show that the solutions $u_p$ converge strongly in $L^2(\Omega)$, uniformly in time, to the solution $u_1$ of the parabolic $1$-Laplace equation as $p\to 1$.
item.dc:creator: Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: Complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for positive $(p,p)$-forms on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2411.06497v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for differential $(p,p)$-forms is introduced on compact K\"ahler manifolds. For any $1 \leq p < n$, we show the existence of smooth solutions unique up to adding constants. For $p=1$, this corresponds to the Calabi-Yau theorem proved by S. T. Yau, and for $p=n-1$, this gives the Monge-Amp\`ere equation for $(n-1)$ plurisubharmonic functions studied by Tosatti-Weinkove. For other $p$ values, this defines a non-linear PDE that falls outside of the general framework of Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck. Further, we define a geometric flow for higher-order forms that extends the K\"ahler-Ricci flow naturally to $(p,p)$-forms. As a consequence of our main theorem, we show that this flow exists in a maximal time interval and can be shown to converge under some assumptions. A modified flow is introduced and the convergence of the associated normalized flow is shown.
item.dc:creator: Mathew George

item.title: Existence and Smoothing for a Nondivergence-Form Degenerate Diffusion from Plasma-Wave Theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.13922v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove existence and positive-time smoothing of weak solutions to the degenerate parabolic Cauchy--Dirichlet problem $\partial_t u = \rho_\lambda(x)u\,\partial_x^2 u + \rho_\lambda(x)g(x)u$ on the half-line, where $\rho_\lambda$ vanishes at the boundary and grows at infinity. This scalar problem arises from a formal reduction of the one-dimensional quasilinear system for plasma waves, which couples an electron distribution to a wave-energy spectrum: we develop a solution theory for the scalar problem that lifts to this system. For the scalar problem, we construct nonnegative weak solutions under weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data and boundedness of the reaction coefficient $\rho_\lambda g$, admitting unbounded and discontinuous data pertinent to the physical model. We establish a one-sided bound on $\partial_t u$ which yields positive-time smoothing: solutions become locally H\"older continuous in both space and time and locally Lipschitz continuous in space. Explicit examples show that this spatial regularity is sharp. Under natural assumptions on the initial data, our scalar solutions lift to weak solutions of the particle--wave system that preserve nonnegativity, conserve particle mass, smooth initial particle measures to locally bounded densities at positive times, and exhibit quantitative decay of the wave spectrum at large wavenumber.
item.dc:creator: William Porteous, Irene M. Gamba, Kun Huang

item.title: Parabolic abstract evolution equations in cylindrical domains and uniformly local Sobolev spaces
item.description: arXiv:2508.05220v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we consider parabolic equations of the type $$\partial_t u(x,t)=\Delta u(x,t) - Bu(x,t) + F(u(x,t))$$ where $u$ is valued in a transverse Hilbert space $Y$ and $B$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on $Y$, allowing a different diffusion mechanism in the transverse direction. We aim at considering solutions with infinite energy and we study the Cauchy problem in the uniformly local spaces associated with the norm $$\|u\|_{L^2_{\text{ul}}(\mathbb{R},Y)}= \sup_{a\in\mathbb{R}^d} \|u(x)\|_{L^2(B(a,1),Y)}.$$ For the classical parabolic equation, i.e. if $Y=\mathbb{R}$, it is known that the Cauchy problem is ill-posed in the weak version of the uniformly local spaces but well-posed in a stronger version, where additional uniform continuity is required. In this paper, we show that the linear operator $\partial^2_{xx} - B$ is not necessarily a sectorial operator in any version of the uniformly local Lebesgue space, due to the possible non-density of its domain. Then, we use the theory of parabolic abstract evolution equations to set a well-posed Cauchy problem, even in the weak version of the uniformly local space. In particular, we believe that this paper offers a new perspective on the comparison between both versions of the uniformly local spaces and also provides a new natural example of differential operators with non-dense domain.
item.dc:creator: Romain Joly

item.title: Hyperbolic $O (N)$ linear sigma model and its mean-field limit
item.description: arXiv:2511.21950v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study large $N$ limits of the hyperbolic $O(N)$ linear sigma model ($\text{HLSM}_N$) on the two-dimensional torus $\mathbb T^2$, namely, a system of $N$ interacting stochastic damped nonlinear wave equations (SdNLW) with coupled cubic nonlinearities. After establishing (pathwise) global well-posedness of $\text{HLSM}_N$ and the limiting equation, called the mean-field SdNLW, we first establish global-in-time convergence of $\text{HLSM}_N$ to the mean-field SdNLW with general initial data (under a suitable assumption). In particular, for the local-in-time convergence, we obtain a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ under an additional integrability assumption on initial data. We then show that the invariant Gibbs dynamics for $\text{HLSM}_N$ converges to that for the mean-field SdNLW with a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ on any large time intervals.
item.dc:creator: Ruoyuan Liu, Shao Liu, Tadahiro Oh

item.title: Stability of the Shape for Circular Vortex Filaments under Non-Symmetric Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2602.18155v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the nonlinear orbital stability of circular vortex filaments governed by the Localized Induction Equation (LIE) under non-symmetric perturbations, within the framework of [Tani-Nishiyama, 1997]. This result extends the first author's recent work [Aiki, 2025] by removing symmetry assumptions on perturbations. While the circular filaments are known to be Lyapunov unstable due to linear growth of the translational mode, we prove that their shape remains globally stable modulo spatial translations and rotations about the symmetry axis. The crucial ingredient is a geometric stability estimate derived from the conservation of vector fluid impulse, which constrains the low-frequency modulations that are not covered by the relative energy. Finally, we relate the fluid impulse to an isoperimetric inequality, yielding a geometric constraint for closed filaments.
item.dc:creator: Masashi Aiki, Mitsuo Higaki

item.title: Fokker-Planck analysis and invariant laws for a continuous-time stochastic model inspired by Adam
item.description: arXiv:2604.00840v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a degenerate stochastic system inspired by bias-corrected Adam. The system arises as the continuous-time limit of an explicitly modified recursion in which the squared-gradient update is replaced by a prescribed second-moment closure. We construct an entrance solution at the singular initial time and prove convergence of the modified recursion on finite time intervals away from zero. Bias correction enters through time-dependent coefficients which converge to constants as time tends to infinity. For a smooth objective with globally Lipschitz gradient and radial dissipativity at infinity, we prove existence and uniqueness of an invariant probability measure for the autonomous system under either $b<4a$ or $\gamma L_f\le a(\sigma/\sqrt2+\varepsilon)/4$. Here $L_f$ is the Lipschitz constant of the gradient, $a,b$ are the relaxation rates, $\gamma$ is the learning-rate parameter, and $\sigma,\varepsilon$ are the noise and regularization parameters. The proof combines an exponential Lyapunov function with compact-set minorization obtained from explicit control paths and a regular endpoint map. Under an exponential Lyapunov moment condition, we obtain exponential convergence in weighted total variation and in the squared $2$-Wasserstein distance of the complete state. The invariant law has finite moments of every order, and qualitative total variation convergence holds for every initial probability law. The time-inhomogeneous process converges weakly to the same invariant law. We formulate the associated Fokker-Planck equation for probability measures and establish local hypoellipticity and smoothness of the invariant density where $\operatorname{Diag}(\nabla f)D^2f$ is invertible. A quadratic example shows that a uniform exponential convergence estimate requires a prefactor growing exponentially in the initial position along a specified family of states.
item.dc:creator: Kaj Nystr\"om

item.title: Lyapunov Unstable Motion Bifurcating from a Circular Vortex Filament
item.description: arXiv:2604.15655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of closed vortex filaments in $\R^3$ governed by the Localized Induction Equation. Recently, Aiki and Higaki (2026) established the nonlinear orbital stability of circular vortex filaments under asymmetric perturbations, while identifying Lyapunov instability due to the linear growth of translation modes. Motivated by this result, we prove the existence of a family of closed solutions, which we call axial screw motions, that bifurcate from a circular filament. These solutions remain uniformly close to the orbit of the circle, but drift secularly away from the reference motion because their translation speed along the symmetry axis differs from that of the circular filament. In particular, they provide explicit non-trivial perturbations that satisfy orbital-stability estimates while failing Lyapunov stability, thereby realizing the gap between orbital stability and Lyapunov stability near the circular filament.
item.dc:creator: Masashi Aiki, Mitsuo Higaki

item.title: Kinetic theory for Transformers and the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon
item.description: arXiv:2605.09213v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study causal self-attention dynamics -- a toy model for decoder Transformers -- which we interpret as a non-exchangeable interacting particle system. Adapting cumulant expansions to the triangular causal dependency structure of the model, and appealing to non-hierarchical methods to estimate correlations using Glauber calculus, we prove a quantitative mean-field limit result and a next-order characterization of correlations. For iid uniformly distributed tokens, the limiting correlation equation can be solved in closed form and we obtain a rigorous explanation of the empirically observed \emph{lost-in-the-middle} phenomenon: the token retrieval profile, as a function of the source position in the prompt, is $\mathsf{U}$-shaped, with primacy, recency, and a unique interior minimum under an explicit smallness condition.
item.dc:creator: Mitia Duerinckx, Borjan Geshkovski, Stefano Rossi

item.title: Asymptotic stability of strong rarefaction waves to a parabolic-hyperbolic system arising from chemotaxis
item.description: arXiv:2606.01559v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We are interested in the asymptotic behavior of solutions toward strong rarefaction waves for a parabolic-hyperbolic system arising from chemotaxis. Suppose that the Riemann problem to the corresponding inviscid system admits rarefaction waves. We show that if the initial data is a small perturbation of an approximate rarefaction wave, then the Cauchy problem has a unique global solution that converges to the rarefaction wave asymptotically in time. The stability results hold regardless of the wave strengths. The waves can be either a single rarefaction wave or a composite of two rarefaction waves. In the composite case, we separate the initial centers of the two approximate profiles to make their interaction error term small while retaining convergence to the prescribed Riemann wave. The proofs are based on the energy method, where the key observations are the monotonicity of the approximate rarefaction waves with respect to both space and time, and the appropriate replacement of spatial derivative of the hyperbolic component with the parabolic component in proper forms.
item.dc:creator: Sitong Liu, Jingyu Li

item.title: Normalized solutions to an exponential growth Choquard equation driven by mixed local-nonlocal operator in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2606.02141v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of normalized solutions to the mixed nonlinear Choquard equation with exponential growth \begin{equation} \left\{ \mathcal{L}u+\lambda u = \Lambda (I_{\alpha}*F(u))f(u) \text{ in }\mathbb{R}^{2}; \;\; \int_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}|u|^{2}\,dx = a^{2}, \right. \end{equation} where $\mathcal{L}=-\Delta+(-\Delta)^s$, $0<s<1$, $a>0$, $I_{\alpha}$ is the Riesz potential of order $\alpha\in(0,2)$, $\Lambda>0$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ arises as a Lagrange multiplier. The nonlinearity has critical exponential growth in the sense of the Trudinger-Moser inequality. Using variational methods, the associated Poho\v{z}aev manifold, and suitable Moser-type estimates, we establish the existence of a normalized solution of mountain-pass type with associated non zero Lagrange multiplier. Under an additional monotonicity assumption on the nonlinearity, we further show that the obtained solution is a normalized ground state. We also establish the regularity properties required for the proof of the corresponding Poho\v{z}aev identity.
item.dc:creator: Nidhi Nidhi, L. Sharma, K. Sreenadh

item.title: Mixed Third-Order Flux Laws for Dual Cascade in the Stochastic SQG Equation
item.description: arXiv:2606.26788v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study dual-cascade flux laws for the stochastic forced--dissipative surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equation on a large periodic box. For statistically stationary solutions, under a weak anomalous dissipation assumption, we derive rigorous mixed third-order structure-function laws for the dual cascade: a Yaglom-type law for the direct cascade of surface potential energy (SPE) and a mixed flux law for the inverse cascade of the Hamiltonian. We further establish complementary scaling laws: a cubic small-scale law for the Hamiltonian structure function and a large-scale vanishing law for the SPE structure function. In particular, both Hamiltonian laws appear to be new for SQG even as an explicit third-order structure-function relation. We also prove Onsager-type obstruction results showing that sufficiently regular stationary families cannot sustain the corresponding non-zero fluxes: $B^s_{3,\infty}$-regularity above the Onsager threshold $1/3$ rules out the direct SPE flux, while sufficient low-frequency Besov regularity rules out the inverse Hamiltonian flux. These results provide a rigorous formulation of the SQG dual-cascade phenomenology in a stochastic stationary setting.
item.dc:creator: Rongchang Liu, Kening Lu, Zexin Wang

item.title: The Follow-the-Leader scheme with non-monotone velocity
item.description: arXiv:2607.28195v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses the approximation of entropy solutions to a one-dimensional scalar conservation law via the so-called Follow-the-Leader particle scheme in case the velocity map is \emph{non monotone}. The result is based on a discrete maximum principle, on $BV$ estimates of the approximated density, and on the characterization of the limit as entropy solution in the sense of Kru\v zkov.
item.dc:creator: Marco Di Francesco

item.title: Quantitative uniqueness for bi-Laplace equations with potentials
item.description: arXiv:2608.08866v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quantitative unique continuation for bi-Laplace equations \[\Delta^{2}u+V(x)u=0 \] by introducing some new weighted frequency functions. We establish quantitative three-ball inequalities and vanishing-order bounds for bounded and H\"older continuous potentials. Three-ball inequalities are built on rescaling invariant weighted frequency functions. The vanishing order results are shown by related, but different weighted frequency functions.
item.dc:creator: Long Teng, Zhiwei Wang, Jiuyi Zhu

item.title: Strauss and Glassey exponents for semilinear wave equations with a non-effective and not scattering producing damping
item.description: arXiv:2608.14311v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problems for a semilinear damped wave equation with a time-dependent coefficient for the damping term belonging to the class of non-effective damping terms with critical decay rates involving iterated logarithmic factors. As nonlinearities we consider both $|u|^p$ and $|u_t|^p$. Assuming nonnegative and compactly supported initial data, we establish the blow-up for weak solutions in the sub-Strauss range $1 < p \leq p_{\mathrm{Str}}(n)$ for the power of the nonlinear term $|u|^p$. The proof in the sub-critical case relies on an iteration frame for the space average of the solution, obtained by employing a time-dependent multiplier related to the coefficient of the damping term. On the other hand, in the limit case $p=p_{\mathrm{Str}}(n)$, we work with solutions of the homogeneous equation with separated variables, and we investigate the properties of a fundamental system of solutions for the corresponding time-dependent ODE, in order to derive an iteration frame for a suitable weighted space average of the solution. Finally, for the derivative type nonlinearity $|u_t|^p$ we prove the blow-up of weak solutions in the sub-Glassey range $1 < p \leq \frac{n+1}{n-1}$ by using a comparison argument for a suitable time-dependent function associated with the corresponding local in time solution.
item.dc:creator: Wanderley Nunes do Nascimento, Alessandro Palmieri

item.title: Fully fractional Schr\"odinger equations with memory: well-posedness via extension
item.description: arXiv:2609.01826v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with memory $\Le^s u=\mu|u|^{p-1}u$ for $t>0$, where $\Le^s=(\partial_t-i\Delta_x)^s$, $0<s<1$, and the solution is prescribed for all $t\le0$. We identify a Hilbert space of histories and prove local well-posedness for $1<p\le p_*(s)=1+4s/(d+2-2s)$, with global solutions for sufficiently small histories at the critical exponent. We also establish the passage from this memory problem to the classical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation as $s\uparrow1$. For every fixed Schwartz history and $1<p\le1+4/d$, including the classical mass critical exponent, the memory solutions converge in $C([0,T];L^2\cap L^{p+1})$ to the classical solution with initial value $u_0(\cdot,0)$, for every finite $T$ below its maximal existence time. Thus the limiting evolution depends on the prescribed past only through its value at time zero. Our construction uses an oscillatory Poisson extension and an exact identity expressing the weighted $L^2$ norm of the lifted initial datum in terms of the history. This identity allows us to apply the boundary estimates of our earlier work to the memory problem. We recover $\Le^s$ as a weighted Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and establish the corresponding extension bounds on $L^2$ for $0<s\le\frac12$, and from $\operatorname{Dom}(\Le^s)$ to $L^2$ for $\frac12<s<1$.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Garofalo, Gigliola Staffilani

item.title: The Shubin--Vakilian--Wolff Uncertainty Principle at Half Density
item.description: arXiv:2609.13958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Shubin, Vakilian, and Wolff proved a Fourier uncertainty principle for sets of sufficiently small local density at the reciprocal scale and asked whether every density below one is admissible. We answer this question negatively in dimension one by constructing sequences of pairs of $1/2$-density thin sets and unit vectors whose total position and Fourier mass outside these sets tends to zero. This obstruction persists for every scaled reciprocal profile $\rho_\kappa(x)=\min\{1,\kappa/|x|\}$, $\kappa>0$. On the other hand, for $0<\kappa\le1$, the uncertainty estimate holds whenever the density $$ \varepsilon<\frac{1}{2(1+32\kappa)}. $$ Thus the critical density tends to $1/2$ as $\kappa\downarrow 0$. The obstruction uses odd Gaussian packets to transfer norm bounds from a free-group model. The positive estimate uses a Fourier-complementary anti-Wick operator and quadratic straightening of the reciprocal geometry.
item.dc:creator: Ming Wang, Yunlei Wang

item.title: Double-wells in a strong magnetic field: absence of tunneling for infinitely many values of the coupling constant
item.description: arXiv:2609.21078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the fixed-potential conjecture of Fefferman, Shapiro, and Weinstein for inversion-symmetric magnetic double wells. We construct a number $L_0>0$ and one smooth, compactly supported, nonpositive, nonradial single-well potential $v$, independent of both the coupling parameter $\lambda$ and the well displacement, such that for every fixed $L\ge L_0$ the associated magnetic double-well Hamiltonian has infinitely many exact degeneracies of its two lowest eigenvalues as $\lambda\to\infty$. The magnetic hopping coefficient also vanishes along an infinite sequence tending to infinity. The potential consists of a radial core and two small, reflection-related perturbations supported on one-sided quadratic cusps. Their log-flat profiles isolate two dominant hopping contributions, which we evaluate by steepest descent after inserting the radial ground-state asymptotics. The resulting asymptotic cosine expression, together with error bounds for the even--odd splitting, yields infinitely many exact eigenvalue crossings and changes of ground-state parity.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Buck, Charles L. Fefferman, Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Amaury Hayat, Jacob Shapiro, Michael I. Weinstein

item.title: Sharp $L^2$ estimates for wave equations with non-integrable speeds
item.description: arXiv:2609.23230v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the large-time behavior of the displacement for wave equations with non-integrable speeds and zero initial displacement. For initial velocities in $L^2\cap L^1$, we derive an $L^2$ upper bound under a weighted Poincar\'e inequality and symbol estimates up to order two on the propagation speed. The rate is determined by the speed and its time integral. For these speeds, an additional symbol estimate for the third derivative and the nonzero mean condition on the initial velocity give a lower bound of the same order, obtained without using an explicit formula for the Fourier multiplier. At the endpoint $a(t)=(1+t)^{-1}$, the sharp rate is $t(\ln t)^{-\frac{n}{4}}$. The estimates apply to polynomial, logarithmically modified, oscillating, and exponential-type speeds.
item.dc:creator: Halit Sevki Aslan, Wenhui Chen

item.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for unregularized Vlasov-Riesz-Fokker-Planck systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.23709v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for the unregularized repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck system on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$. For product initial data and potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$, we obtain an algebraic convergence rate for the $k$-particle marginals on a time interval independent of the particle number. The constants grow at most exponentially in $k$. The three-dimensional Coulomb case gives every rate $N^{-b}$ with $0<b<1/3$. The assumptions on its limiting solution hold for weighted Sobolev data with a Gaussian velocity moment and, on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a polynomial spatial moment. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law, auxiliary particle equations, and weighted BBGKY estimates. An $L^1$ estimate and pointwise exponential energy bounds control the remainder flux in weighted $L^q$. For correlated initial data satisfying pointwise energy and marginal error bounds, the comparison extends to $0<s<d-1$.
item.dc:creator: Ning Jiang, Juntao Wu

item.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic half-wave equation on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2609.24930v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct global solutions of the defocusing cubic half-wave equation on the torus whose $H^s$ norms grow exponentially for every $1/2<s<3/2$. Such solutions exist at every positive mass. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first example of a genuine infinite cascade for a defocusing fractional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the torus. In particular, our result resolves an open question posed by G\'erard and Grellier concerning the existence of unbounded Sobolev trajectories for the defocusing cubic half-wave equation on the torus.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen

item.title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15457v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation and the constant quadratic Hessian equation, based on the two-point maximum principle. The arguments require only one differentiation of the equation. For the Monge-Amp\`ere equation, the inhomogeneous term is assumed to be positive and continuously differentiable. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Jui-Yun Hung, Jiakun Liu, Neil Trudinger

item.title: Multi-dimensional centered rarefaction waves of gas dynamics with vacuum states
item.description: arXiv:2610.18177v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the local-in-time structural stability of two centered rarefaction waves bounding a vacuum region for the two-dimensional isentropic Euler equations with $p(\rho)=k\rho^\gamma$, for $\gamma\in(1,1.3]\cup\{\frac75,\frac53\}$. For general sufficiently small perturbations of the planar Riemann data, allowing nonzero vorticity, we construct an entropy solution that is continuous for positive time and whose five regions are separated by four characteristic surfaces. The conservative solution has uniform spatial $W^{2,\infty}$ bounds on each time slice of the central region in coordinates $(x_1/t,x_2)$; for $\gamma=7/5,5/3$, we also obtain spacetime $W^{2,\infty}$ regularity in $(t,x_1/t,x_2)$. The proof develops characteristic geometry directly for the symmetric first-order Euler system and uses two overlapping characteristic charts to separate matching with the exterior flow from estimates uniform up to vacuum. Fixed commutators without sound-speed weights exhibit a first-order null structure, while subtraction of explicit approximate solutions produces damping that cancels the leading antidamping bulk terms in the energy identity. An explicit analysis of the initial-slice ODEs identifies fractional powers and logarithmic terms at zero sound speed. The logarithmic coefficients couple vorticity to tangential variation of the initial data, revealing an obstruction to higher spatial regularity even when the powers of the sound speed have integer exponents. This analysis determines the finite approximation order used to close the energy and geometric estimates in the stated range. These ingredients provide the geometric and energy framework for the forthcoming second paper of this series, which will use finite evolving profiles to treat the full range $\gamma\in(1,\frac53]$.
item.dc:creator: Jin Jia, Tao Luo

item.title: Hardy-Sobolev-Maz'ya inequalities for $\boldsymbol{1<p<2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.22540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9].
