These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.
item.dc:creator: Avas Banerjee, Micha{\l} Kijaczko, Vivek Sahu

item.title: On one-dimensional pressureless Euler--Poisson systems: existence for non-semiconvex interaction potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.25754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are repulsive at short range and attractive at long range are useful simplified models that describe biological aggregation. In the current work we employ new techniques to treat compactly supported solutions in the case where the potential is $C^1$ and satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions although it is not necessarily semiconvex, as required in previous work. Central to this approach are uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system, which requires the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. In the semiconvex case, these bounds also yield convergence of time-shifted trajectories to an eternal solution. The tradeoff, just as in the case of repulsive Euler-Poisson, is that we cannot claim that the emerging solutions for non-semiconvex potentials are sticky.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Xie, Emmanuel Alayande, Christopher Chun, Yusen Li, Rohan Mawalkar, Adrian Tudorascu, Adam Van

item.title: A double-logarithmic lifespan bound for axisymmetric Euler equations with a small initial swirl
item.description: arXiv:2610.25888v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the axisymmetric incompressible Euler equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a small initial swirl. Fix $s>7/2$, and let $\boldsymbol{v}_0\in H^s(\mathbb{R}^3)$ be axisymmetric and divergence-free. If $\varepsilon=\|{\nabla\times(v_{0,\theta}\boldsymbol{e}_{\theta})}\|_{L^\infty}$ is sufficiently small, then the lifespan $T_*$ of the corresponding $H^s$ solution satisfies $$ T_{*}\geq\frac{C_s}{1+\|{\boldsymbol{v}_0}\|_{H^s}} \left[ \log\log (\varepsilon^{-1}) \right]^{3/7}\,. $$ This removes the assumption by Danchin (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 141:1979-1993, 2013) that the domain must be distant from the axis of symmetry. Moreover, even for $\boldsymbol{v}_0\in H^3$, our result improves the fourfold iterated-logarithmic lower bound for the lifespan obtained by Li and Zhou (Z. Angew. Math. Phys. 75:219, 2024) to a threefold iterated-logarithmic bound.
item.dc:creator: Zijin Li, Xu Xiao, Linbin Yang

item.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28572v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(\Delta_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Castellanos

item.title: Variational structure of Fokker-Planck equations with variable mobility
item.description: arXiv:2505.10676v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Fokker--Planck equations with symmetric, positive definite mobility matrices capturing diffusion in heterogeneous environments. A weighted Wasserstein metric is introduced for which these equations are gradient flows. This metric is shown to emerge from an optimal control problem in the space of probability densities for a class of variable mobility matrices, with the cost function capturing the work dissipated via friction. Using the Nash-Kuiper isometric embedding theorem for Riemannian manifolds, we demonstrate the existence of optimal transport maps. Additionally, we construct a time-discrete variational scheme, establish key properties for the associated minimizing problem, and prove convergence to weak solutions of the associated Fokker-Planck equation.
item.dc:creator: Hailiang Liu, Athanasios E. Tzavaras

item.title: Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations
item.description: arXiv:2505.14012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and long-time behavior of a general continuum neural field model with Gaussian noise on possibly unbounded domains. In particular, we give conditions for the existence of invariant probability measures by restricting the solution flow to an invariant subspace with a nonlocal metric. Under the assumption of a sufficiently large decay parameter relative to the noise intensity, the norm of the connectivity kernel operator, and the Lipschitz regularity of the activation function, we establish exponential ergodicity and exponential mixing of the associated Markovian Feller semigroup and the uniqueness of the invariant measure.
item.dc:creator: Anna-Mariya Otsetova, Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: Absolute continuity of the law of the solution to the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation driven by fractional noise
item.description: arXiv:2601.10490v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The stochastic partial differential equation analyzed in this work is the Cahn-Hilliard equation perturbed by an additive fractional white noise (fractional in time and white in space). We work in spatial dimensions $d \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ with $d < 4H$, where $H \in (\frac{1}{2}, 1)$ is the Hurst parameter of the noise, and apply Malliavin calculus to investigate the existence of a density for the solution $u$. In particular, we show that $u$ admits a jointly continuous modification and construct a localizing sequence through which we prove that its Malliavin derivative exists locally, and that its law is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$, thereby establishing that a density exists. We obtain the result for the whole range of dimensions and Hurst parameters in which the mild solution is known to exist. The analysis rests on three new estimates. The first bounds the expectation of the $p$-th power ($p \geq 2$) of the $L^{\infty}(D)$-norm of the stochastic integral appearing in the mild formulation. The other two concern the integral involving the operator associated with the kernel that appears in the integral representation of the fractional noise: an upper estimate and, more importantly, a lower estimate on short time intervals, which yields the nondegeneracy of the Malliavin derivative.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Dimitriou, Dimitris Farazakis, Georgia Karali

item.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2609.19052v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(\Omega) \le \frac{\pi^{s-\frac{1}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)\Gamma\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partial\Omega)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
